tier_reason: The string-index-benchmarks README tables (artifact results/frontier-1m-2026-09-26-arz-be75a38.json) show lexindex DictIndex 1024 smallest on 13 of 13 corpora at 1M keys (words 2.51 vs MARISA rho=2 2.98, titles-en 7.21 vs 8.19) and HashedDictIndex closed at 14 to 61 ns vs XCDAT 15 at 54 to 449 ns; harness code is public (harness/build.sh compiles MARISA and XCDAT with c++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++17, -DNDEBUG for XCDAT and the floor/resident drivers), toolchain GCC 16.2.1 / rustc 1.98.1 and CPU AMD Ryzen 7 5800HS are stated.

corrections.caveats: Harness author is the lexindex author (conflict of interest, disclosed in the README; harness pins every competitor, fetches lexindex 4.5.2 from crates.io and publishes JSON artifacts). The 14 to 61 ns closed HashedDictIndex lookup returns some id for keys that were never inserted, so it is not equivalent to the tries' exact search. lexindex's fastest exact search trails XCDAT 15 on 9 of 13 corpora at 1M keys (5 percent on uuid to 57 percent on pypi), wins dna (0.95x) and numeric (0.55x); at 10M keys it wins dna, numeric, urls and titles-en and loses opaque (1.36x). Against MARISA at its smallest (1 to 32 tries, tiny cache, untimed) the size margin shrinks to 0.04 percent on paths and 3.8 percent on titles-en at 1M, 0.11 to 0.30 percent on titles-en/urls at 10M, and MARISA is smaller once loaded (mmap) on five rows. The numeric corpus win (301 bytes total) is a degenerate dense-id case. Baselines are succinct tries (MARISA, XCDAT, CoCo-trie, PDT, FST, C2 variants), not SDSL or sux directly. String-index-benchmarks repo has 0 stars.

notes: All quoted numbers match the README tables of ilgrad/string-index-benchmarks. Metadata matches the lexindex repo page (MIT, 3 stars, latest commits 2026-09-29). Main claim is size; speed wins are confined to the closed-lookup variant and a few corpora.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Space: paper abstract (search snippet) reports 0.78 percent overhead, 4.5x to 64.1x less than previous implementations. Checked-in logs (1e9 bits, density 0.5, 2e7 random select_1 queries, i9-13900H): m3 overhead 0.82 percent vs simple_s1 2.34, pasta flat 3.58, simple_s3 7.03, sdsl_mcl 23.63, rank9sel 56.25, sdsl_sd 78.15 percent (2.9x to 95x less overhead, derived from page data). Query time is not a win: m3 100.4 ns vs simple_s1 100.2, rank9sel 100.3, sdsl_mcl 80.9, simple_s3 49.1 ns in the same run; a second run gives m3 95 to 96 ns (0.82 percent config) or 77 to 79 ns (3.2 percent config) vs 76 to 185 ns for competitors depending on density.
corrections.hardware: 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900H (from checked-in log lines)
corrections.caveats: Paper (arXiv 2509.17819, Kurpicz, Rigi-Luperti, Sanders) is blocked here; its 4.5x to 64.1x figure comes from a search snippet. The checked-in logs are single-instance, single-iteration example runs (the README calls the script an exemplary benchmark) and include one run tagged 'vb', apparently a virtual machine. The claim is about space overhead; at the 0.82 percent setting select_1 is level with rank9sel and simple_select s1 and about 2x slower than simple_select s3 and slower than SDSL mcl. Reproduction script clones competitor repos (sdsl-lite, sux, rankselect, rankselect2) at their heads, not pinned commits.

notes: Found real numbers in the repo's multibench_out logs, so tier goes C to A for the space claim; speed is not faster. Metadata matches (MPL-2.0 per README/LICENSE.md, 5 stars, last commit 2026-09-15 README edit, code last changed 2025-09-21).
